candidates.name: Climate/weather operational exposure
candidates.next_gate: geographic exposure map + weather publication/PIT contract
candidates.hypothesis: An exogenous weather shock may alter operations, transport, energy usage or regional demand for geographically concentrated firms.
candidates.construction: Freeze a public geographic exposure map from issuer disclosures and combine it with NOAA/NCEI observations available before the next eligible session; later location changes and future returns cannot rewrite the map.

candidates.name: Electricity load imbalance × industrial exposure
candidates.next_gate: release/vintage treatment for continuously updated EIA series
candidates.hypothesis: Unusual electricity demand or power-system stress may propagate differently to electricity-intensive industries.
candidates.construction: Use a fixed load/deviation state from a documented EIA public release or frozen vintage boundary and a lagged industrial exposure map; continuous API updates are never treated as a historical clock.

candidates.name: Petroleum inventory shock × sector sensitivity
candidates.next_gate: release schedule and revision-aware inventory contract
candidates.hypothesis: Energy-inventory surprises may affect transportation, chemicals, refiners and other sectors asymmetrically.
candidates.construction: Use a fixed EIA inventory state and predeclared sector exposure classes; preserve the publication schedule and a revision-aware vintage policy without threshold optimization.

candidates.name: Federal procurement shock × public contractor
candidates.next_gate: transaction/amendment and public dissemination timestamp contract
candidates.hypothesis: Unusually large or newly started federal awards may create an information event for listed contractors.
candidates.construction: Construct fixed award-event classes from USAspending transaction/award identities and public dissemination timestamps, with issuer/CIK mapping frozen before the decision period and amendments separated.

candidates.name: Legal docket intensity × issuer
candidates.next_gate: coverage census and next-session observation boundary
candidates.hypothesis: Abnormal public litigation activity may alter issuer-specific uncertainty or information-processing conditions.
candidates.construction: Use a fixed daily count/state of newly observable public proceedings for a pre-registered issuer set; use the next-session boundary unless a more exact public timestamp is proven, and do not assume universal court coverage.

candidates.name: Regulatory/enforcement shock
candidates.next_gate: fixed event taxonomy and release-time contract
candidates.hypothesis: A newly public regulatory or enforcement event may create an exogenous issuer information state.
candidates.construction: Use a fixed SEC/CFTC/government event taxonomy and explicit release-time contract; duplicate/amended events and entity mappings remain separate and no NLP sentiment or return-based classification is introduced at feasibility stage.
